full_text:
We finally made it to the [2026 NFL Draft](https://www.fantasypoints.com/nfl/series/2026/nfl-draft#/), and there’s plenty of fallout from the three-day event. This year’s rookie class is getting most of the spotlight, but the selection of the top prospects will also have a huge impact on their new teammates for the upcoming season. Let’s dive in to see which veteran players are looking better and which are looking worse for the 2026 fantasy season based on the results of the NFL Draft.

\>Be sure to check out the [2026 NFL Prospect Guide](https://www.fantasypoints.com/nfl/prospect-guide#/) for detailed scouting reports on the rookie prospects from Brett Whitefield…This article is powered by [*Fantasy Points Data*](https://data.fantasypoints.com/). Subscribe [now](https://www.fantasypoints.com/plans#/) to take your research to the next level….ADP in this article is courtesy of Underdog Fantasy.

{{CTA|Underdog|omit=\[none\]}}

__PLAYERS WHO AVOIDED DRAFT LANDMINES__
---------------------------------------

#### Running Backs

__{{Tony Pollard|RB|Ten|20912}}__ (Ten) — The Titans didn’t get the chance to select Jeremiyah Love at No. 4. Pollard’s ADP (110.6, RB36) will rise by a round or two over the next couple of weeks. The Titans selected Penn State’s Nicholas Singleton in the fifth round, but he’ll have work to do to earn touches behind Pollard and Tyjae Spears.

__{{Cam Skattebo|RB|NYG|25887}}__ (NYG) — Skattebo remains atop New York’s depth chart after the Cardinals selected Jeremiyah Love third overall. The Giants even upgraded their offensive line by selecting Francis Mauigoa 10th overall.

__{{Chase Brown|RB|CIN|24374}}__ (Cin) — Brown still has the 30-year-old Samaje Perine as his top backup after the Bengals failed to do anything of note in the draft and free agency.

__{{Aaron Jones|RB|MIN}}__ and __{{Jordan Mason|RB|MIN|23364}}__ (Min) — The Vikings will run it back with the tandem of Jones and Mason in their backfield after passing on RBs through the first five rounds of the draft.

__{{Rachaad White|RB|WAS|23217}}__ and __{{Jacory Croskey-Merritt|RB|WAS|26259}}__ (Was) — White and JCM still have the inside track to lead this backfield after the Commanders waited until the sixth round to select Penn State’s Kaytron Allen.

#### Wide Receivers & Tight Ends

__{{Rashee Rice|WR|KC|24120}}__ (KC) — The Chiefs upgraded their defense and passed on selecting a WR with their two first-round picks.

__{{Kyle Pitts|TE|ATL|22508}}__ (Atl) — Pitts found himself in trade rumors leading up to the draft, but it appears he’ll stick in Atlanta’s thin receiving corps as the #2 option behind Drake London.

__{{Mark Andrews|TE|BAL|19803}}__ (Bal) — The Ravens let Isaiah Likely walk in free agency and didn’t select a TE until the 133rd overall pick (Matthew Hibner), which leaves Durham Smythe as the #2 TE.

__{{Jalen Nailor|WR|LV|23368}}__ and __{{Tre Tucker|WR|LV|24177}}__ (LV) — The Raiders had one of the biggest needs at WR entering the draft, and passed on the position with their first seven picks.

__{{Josh Downs|WR|IND|24145}}__ (Ind) — Downs has the chance to play in more 2-WR sets after the departure of __Michael Pittman__, and the Colts waited until their final pick of the draft in the seventh round to select a WR (Deion Burks).

__{{Isaac TeSlaa|WR|DET|26101}}__ (Det) — The Lions remained committed to TeSlaa as their #3 WR, adding just __Greg Dortch__ in free agency and declining to add any significant rookie WR competition in the draft.

__{{Jake Tonges|TE|SF|23662}}__ (SF) — San Francisco passed on the TE position in the draft, which leaves Tonges as the 49ers' TE to roster for as long as George Kittle is on the mend from an Achilles that he suffered in January.

__UPGRADES__
------------

*Players whom I’m feeling more optimistic about based on the selections and trades coming out of the 2026 NFL Draft.*

### QUARTERBACKS

__{{Cam Ward|QB|TEN|25323}}__ (Ten) — The Titans are determined to give Ward the best chance at success in his second season following an uneven rookie year after they selected him first overall in 2025. They’ve invested heavily in Ward’s future this offseason by handing __Wan’Dale Robinson__ $38 million guaranteed and selecting Ohio State’s __Carnell Tate__ fourth overall. Robinson is a zone beater in the middle of the field and is dangerous after the catch, with 444 of his receiving yards coming with the ball in his hands, which should help Ward get the ball out of his hands quickly. Brett Whitefield ranked Tate directly between __A.J. Brown__ and __CeeDee Lamb__ as a top-10 WR evaluation in his decade of scouting college prospects. Ward threw for 2 TD passes, and the Titans averaged 26.8 PPG in each of his last four full starts after a rocky start to his rookie campaign. He also led Tennessee to a touchdown on the opening drive against the playoff-bound Jaguars in the season finale before leaving early with a shoulder injury. Ward isn’t getting much respect in early drafts (142.3, QB25), but I suspect that he’ll slightly rise up draft boards this summer.

__{{Tyler Shough|QB|NO|23187}}__ (NO) — I correctly mocked the Saints to select Arizona State’s __Jordyn Tyson__ at No. 8. My rationale was that New Orleans needed to determine if Shough is the quarterback of the future. They needed to put more weapons around him to get a proper evaluation. Mission accomplished. Tyson was one of the late risers in the draft process despite concerns about durability and effort. Brett Whitefield [saw](https://www.fantasypoints.com/nfl/prospect-guide/profiles/rookie/wr#/) shades of __CeeDee Lamb__ in Tyson’s play style, but he believes he needs some developmental runway to reach his full potential. He’ll get to learn on the job from 2022 first-round pick __Chris Olave__, and he significantly upgrades a WR corps that features just __Devuaghn Vele__, __Mason Tipton__, and __Bub Means__ behind Olave. The Saints added Georgia’s __Oscar Delp__ in the third round and North Dakota State’s __Bryce Lance__ in the fourth round to bolster a weak receiving corps. Shough reached 17.1+ FP and 239+ passing yards in seven of his final eight starts despite a weak receiving corps behind Olave, ranking as the QB9 (18.8) from Week 10 on. Shough is currently one of the better bargains (118.7, QB20) at the position, playing in __Kellen Moore__’s fantasy-friendly offense.

__{{Geno Smith|WR|NYJ|14895}}__ (NYJ) — Geno is getting one last chance to be a full-time starter before the Jets try to find a franchise quarterback next offseason after the Rams shocked the league by selecting __Ty Simpson__ 13th overall. Not only did the Jets fail to land Simpson, but they drafted Geno a pair of weapons in Oregon’s __Kenyon Sadiq__ (No. 16) and Indiana’s __Omar Cooper__ (No. 31) to go along with __Garrett Wilson__. Brett Whitefield [described](https://www.fantasypoints.com/nfl/prospect-guide/profiles/rookie/wr#/) Sadiq as a mutant who has the necessary receiving chops to be one of the NFL’s top TEs, and Cooper is a run-after-catch demon who is reminiscent of __D.J. Moore__. Geno finished last in INTs (17) and second to last in sack rate (10.6%) and pressure-to-sack rate (26.7%) among 45 QBs who attempted 100+ passes. Geno deserved plenty of blame for Las Vegas’ offensive issues, but his O-line was a disaster, __Chip Kelly__ was fired mid-season, and he never really had __Brock Bowers__ and __Jakobi Meyers__ at full strength at the same time. The Jets selected Clemson’s __Cade Klubnik__ early in the fourth round, but he should only see the starting lineup if the Jets fall out of contention late in the season. Smith could have a small bounce-back season behind a better offensive line and an improved receiving corps after the draft, and he’s dirt cheap (166, QB29) at the moment.

{{PAYWALL}}

__{{Drake Maye|QB|NE|24958}}__ (NE) — The Patriots continue to build up the offensive line in front of Maye, spending a first-round pick on an offensive tackle for the second straight year. The Patriots slid up three spots to select Utah’s __Caleb Lomu__ at No. 28, which comes a year after they selected __Will Campbell__ fourth overall. Dane Brugler [wrote](https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/interactive/the-beast-2026/player/caleb-lomu-utah-offensive-tackle/) that Lomu has a starting left tackle skill set if he continues to get stronger and improves his technique, and Campbell could eventually slide inside to guard once Lomu is ready to play. New England reached the Super Bowl despite allowing the second-highest pressure rate (43.9%) and the ninth-highest sack rate (7.8%). It’s also looking more likely that the Eagles will trade __A.J. Brown__ in June after Philadelphia moved up to select __Makai Lemon__ to pair with __DeVonta Smith__. The Patriots are the massive favorites to be Brown’s team for the 2026 at 82% on Kalshi, ahead of the Rams (10%) and Eagles (9%). Maye is a small value in early drafts with an ADP of 70.3 (QB7).

__{{Shedeur Sanders|QB|CLE|26079}}__ and __{{Deshaun Watson|QB|CLE|18857}}__ (Cle) — The Browns passed on selecting __Ty Simpson__ at No. 9, and instead bolstered the personnel around their 2026 quarterbacks. Cleveland completed its offensive line overhaul by selecting Utah’s __Spencer Fano__ before adding Texas A&M’s __K.C. Concepcion__ at No. 24. Cleveland allowed the highest pressure rate (44.8%) and the seventh-highest sack rate (8%) last season, so it acquired __Elgton Jenkins__, __Tytus Howard__, and __Zion Johnson__ this offseason before finishing the job by selecting Fano. Brett Whitefield [called](https://www.fantasypoints.com/nfl/prospect-guide/profiles/rookie/ol#/) him one of the premier offensive tackle prospects and elite in pass protection, and he saw shades of __Brandon Aiyuk__ in Concepcion because of his dynamic ability after the catch. Concepcion will eventually compete with __Harold Fannin__ to be the #1 option in Cleveland’s passing game. The Browns added their potential #3 target in the early second round when Washington’s __Denzel Boston__ slid to them at No. 39. They selected Arkansas’ __Taylen Green__ at the start of the sixth round, who is more of a long-term project at the position. Watson is the slight favorite to be the Week 1 starter over Sanders at 50% to 47% on Kalshi. Both quarterbacks will get opportunities to start games. They’re both off the fantasy radar entering the season, but at least Cleveland’s offensive environment improved after the first day of the draft.

__{{Jaxson Dart|QB|NYG|26082}}__ (NYG) — It wasn’t a perfect draft weekend for New York’s second-year quarterback, but the Giants still upgraded his cast on the first two days of the draft. They passed on selecting __Jordyn Tyson__ or another receiver with the fifth and 10th overall picks. Still, they at least beefed up his offensive line by drafting Miami’s __Francis Mauigoa__ at No. 10. Brett Whitefield wrote that Mauigoa is technically sound in pass pro and an extremely high-floor prospect. He should help limit the number of blue tent visits that Dart takes this season. New York finally got around to getting Dart a receiver in the third round when they picked Notre Dame’s __Malachi Fields__, who gives New York insurance if __Malik Nabers__ isn’t ready for the start of the season. Whitefield believes Fields has the potential to be a __Michael Pittman__\-type X-receiver. Dart accounted for 18.6+ FP and multiple TDs in 10 of his first 12 NFL starts, but he’s being drafted in the early eighth round as the QB11.

### RUNNING BACKS

__{{Derrick Henry|RB|BAL|17959}}__ (Bal) — The Ravens need to rebuild the interior of their offensive line after letting __Tyler Linderbaum__ walk in free agency. Luckily for Baltimore, one of the best players in the draft, regardless of position, fell to them at 14th overall, where they selected __Olaivavega Ioane__ out of Penn State. Ioane fell to Baltimore because he plays guard, but he’s exactly what the team needs. Brett Whitefield [called](https://www.fantasypoints.com/nfl/prospect-guide/profiles/rookie/ol#/) Ioane a “premier run-mauler” among guards, and he’ll help Henry remain a force at 33 years old. King Henry is coming off another strong showing as the RB8 with 16.6 FPG, but his efficiency slipped a bit from 2024 when he finished as the RB4 with 19.8 FPG. Henry dipped in stuff rate (38.2%>45%), explosive run rate (7.7%>6.8%), and YBCO/ATT (3.28>2.80) from 2024 to 2025. Henry will eventually show significant signs of decline, but Ioane will help soften that decline for the time being.

__{{Kyren Williams|RB|LAR|23212}}__ and __{{Blake Corum|RB|LAR|24116}}__ (LAR) — The Rams were rumored late to have some interest in trading up for __Jeremiyah Love__, and they also passed on __Makai Lemon__ to select __Ty Simpson__ at No. 13. They selected yet another TE in Ohio State’s __Max Klare__ with their next pick in the second round instead of adding to their extremely thin WR corps. The Rams already have __Terrance Ferguson__, __Colby Parkinson__, __Tyler Higbee__, and __Davis Allen__ under contract for 2026. Los Angeles easily led the league in 13 personnel rate (3 TEs) at 30.5%, which is likely to continue in 2026 with Klare added to the mix. The Rams easily paced the NFL in attempts (204), rushing yards (973), and rushing TDs (12) out of 13 personnel. They also led the league in YPC (4.77) among the 19 teams that attempted at least 40+ carries from the grouping. Los Angeles should have one of the league’s more efficient rushing attacks in a high-scoring offense once again. Williams (35.8, RB17) and Corum (99.7, RB34) are boring but sharp picks at their current ADPs.

__{{David Montgomery|RB|HOU|20882}}__ (Hou) — Montgomery requested a trade after his opportunities dipped once __Dan Campbell__ took over playcalling in Week 10, and his fantasy outlook has significantly improved since Detroit granted his wish and sent him to Houston. He failed to reach 200+ carries and 800+ rushing yards in each of the last two seasons after hitting those marks in each of his first five seasons with the Lions and Bears. Monty is Houston’s latest hired hand at the position, following in __Joe Mixon__’s path from the 2024 season. Mixon ranked as the RB10 with 17.2 FPG in his only season as Houston’s lead back, averaging 17.5 carries and 2.6 receptions per game. Montgomery could be headed toward a similar workload with just __Woody Marks__ challenging for touches. Houston continued to beef up its offensive line by selecting Georgia Tech’s __Keylan Rutledge__ at No. 26, which comes after it acquired __Braden Smith__ and __Wyatt Teller__ earlier this offseason. Houston’s offensive line needed a significant upgrade after ranking 30th in adjusted YBC/ATT (1.45) and 30th in success rate (45.1%). Monty’s ADP has skyrocketed from 107 (RB35) on March 1 to 51.4 (RB21) at the start of the draft, and he could push into the fourth round later this summer.

__{{Quinshon Judkins|RB|CLE|25946}}__ (Cle) — Judkins is well on the road to recovery from the dislocated ankle and fractured fibula he suffered in late December. He [was on the field](https://x.com/camijustice/status/2046631987285299664?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw%7Ctwcamp%5Etweetembed%7Ctwterm%5E2046631987285299664%7Ctwgr%5E25aaf109bf96a0682e957deaafd60837269a7152%7Ctwcon%5Es1_c10&ref_url=https%3A%2F%2Fbrownswire.usatoday.com%2Fstory%2Fsports%2Fnfl%2Fbrowns%2F2026%2F04%2F21%2Fbrowns-receive-positive-update-on-star-rb-quinshon-judkins%2F89719153007%2F) for Cleveland’s voluntary minicamp practice on April 21, which validated GM __Andrew Berry__’s update from late March that Judkins would participate in offseason workouts in some fashion. Judkins should be a full participant in training camp, barring a setback, and the Browns notably let __Jerome Ford__ (Was) walk in free agency while not adding another back. Cleveland completed an overhaul of its offensive line by selecting Utah’s __Spencer Fano__ at No. 9, which comes after it acquired __Elgton Jenkins__, __Tytus Howard__, and __Zion Johnson__ earlier this offseason. Cleveland’s offensive line ranked last in adjusted YBC/ATT (1.14) and second to last in success rate (43%). Brett Whitefield [called](https://www.fantasypoints.com/nfl/prospect-guide/profiles/rookie/ol#/) Fano one of the premier offensive tackle prospects and a dominant run blocker in zone concepts. Cleveland still has one of the league’s worst quarterback situations, but Judkins should at least find more running room after ranking 59th out of 65 RBs in YBCO/ATT (1.36) as a rookie.

__{{Chuba Hubbard|RB|CAR|21691}}__ (Car) — Hubbard’s stock continues to rise heading into 2026 after the Panthers selected Georgia’s __Monroe Freeling__ 19th overall. Carolina chose to bolster its offensive line and pass on __Makai Lemon__ or another receiver. Brett Whitefield [described](https://www.fantasypoints.com/nfl/prospect-guide/profiles/rookie/ol#/) Freeling as an athletic freak with a high ceiling who needs more playing experience to reach his full potential. Carolina previously allowed __Rico Dowdle__ to leave for Pittsburgh in free agency, which left a pair of unproven options in __Jonathon Brooks__ and __Trevor Etienne__, and their 29 combined career carries behind Hubbard. Chuba finished as the RB13 (16.3 FPG) as the lead back in 2024 before falling to RB40 (8.4) while dealing with injuries and Dowdle last season. He’s a bounce-back candidate with a much better setup for 2026, and his ADP is much cheaper this offseason (72.9, RB27).

### RECEIVERS

__{{DeVonta Smith|WR|PHI|21687}}__ and __{{A.J. Brown|WR|PHI|21042}}__ (Phi) — I don’t know what else needs to happen to confirm that Brown won’t be playing for the Eagles this season after __Howie Roseman__ jumped to No. 20 to steal __Makai Lemon__ from the Steelers. The Eagles previously traded for __Dontayvion Wicks__ and signed __Hollywood Brown__ before the draft, and A.J. Brown’s cap hit will drop from $43 million to $16.4 million if he’s traded after June 1. Smith will be the clear top option for the first time in his career, and he’ll be asked to play more on the perimeter with Lemon operating as the primary slot WR, which is a good thing with __Jalen Hurts__ at quarterback. Smith ran 58% of his routes from the slot last season, and Hurts ranked 35th out of 36 QBs on the [rate of throws over the middle of the field](https://x.com/ffdataroma/status/2047673161395716566?s=20) at 16.3%. Smith averaged 6.7/79.7 receiving and 9.7 targets per game for 16.6 FPG in three non-Week 18 contests without Brown the last two seasons. Brown will also likely be in a better position for fantasy success wherever he lands. He’ll likely move to a more pass-happy attack where he won’t be competing against a WR of Smith’s caliber for targets.

__{{Brock Bowers|TE|LV|24943}}__ (LV) — The Raiders landed __Fernando Mendoza__, the top quarterback in this year’s draft, with the first overall pick, who will be a significant upgrade for Las Vegas’ dismal passing attack. The Raiders ranked 28th in passer rating (81.5), 25th in off-target throw percentage (17.9%), and 31st in INTs (19) with __Geno Smith__ struggling in __Chip Kelly__’s lackluster offense. Bowers saw his YPRR (2.11>1.80), TPRR (.27>.22), and FPG (15.5>14.7) fall from his rookie year to his sophomore season. Mendoza heads to Las Vegas off a Heisman Trophy-winning season in which he led Indiana to its first-ever national championship. Brett Whitefield [put Mendoza](https://www.fantasypoints.com/nfl/prospect-guide/profiles/rookie/qb) in a class with __Trevor Lawrence__ and __Joe Burrow__ as the best QB prospects of this decade. Bowers will be in a much better position to succeed with Mendoza and __Kirk Cousins__ running the show in an offense orchestrated by __Klint Kubiak__, who is coming off a Lombardi Trophy as Seattle’s offensive coordinator. Bowers could be featured like __Jaxon Smith-Njigba__ was in Kubiak’s offense last season, and he’s facing little target competition from a WR depth chart led by __Jalen Nailor__. Bowers has a much better chance of living up to his ADP (23.8, TE2), and he’s being drafted a little later than he was last summer.

__{{Jayden Reed|WR|GB|23233}}__ (GB) — Reed’s great month of April continued on draft weekend. The Packers thinned out their WR corps when they traded __Dontayvion Wicks__ in mid-April, and they committed to Reed by handing him a three-year, $50.25 million extension, which included $20 million guaranteed. Green Bay also didn’t select a receiver through the first two days of the draft, leaving __Christian Watson__, Reed, and __Matthew Golden__ as the clear top three WRs. Reed posted a 58% route share last season, and he’s never topped a 68% route share in his four-year career. Reed actually has hope for a bigger role in 2026 based on his contract extension and Green Bay’s thinning receiving corps, so his ADP (100.2, WR45) should continue to rise as it has throughout the offseason.

__DOWNGRADES__
--------------

*Players whom we’re feeling less optimistic about based on the selections and trades coming out of the 2026 NFL Draft.*

### QUARTERBACKS

__{{Patrick Mahomes|QB|KC|18890}}__ (KC) — Kansas City’s days of being the league’s most pass-heavy team could be coming to an end. The Chiefs have ranked inside the top two spots in pass rate over expectation in each of the last five seasons, but they’ve committed to running the ball and to playing better defense this offseason. The Chiefs passed on upgrading Mahomes’ offensive line and his receiving corps through the first two days of the draft by selecting three defensive players inside the top-40 picks. Kansas City also finally had enough of its pathetic rushing attack, handing __Kenneth Walker__ $28.7 million guaranteed in free agency to balance its offense. Mahomes will be in a race to be ready for the start of the season off his ACL and LCL in mid-December, and it wouldn’t be surprising if he gets off to a sluggish start. He is also coming off a career-best 5.2 FPG as a runner last season, which should plummet dramatically since he’s returning from a major knee injury. Mahomes is one of the worst picks on the board at his current ADP (89.8, QB12).

![](STATIC_ASSET_URI/photos/45d92911d5c0126f5f193d18efef85efd18d3617/cc73e6ecaee22c7a41b4244d882800d4de53f2c8)

__{{Matthew Stafford|QB|LAR|9038}}__ (LAR) — The Rams pulled off the surprise pick of the Draft at No. 13, passing on upgrading a Super Bowl-caliber starting roster (the Rams ranked first in my pre-Draft [Power Rankings](https://www.fantasypoints.com/nfl/articles/betting/2026/nfl-power-rankings-post-free-agency#/)) to select __Ty Simpson__ to be Stafford’s backup for the 2026 season. Stafford is on a year-to-year with his playing career entering his age-38, but the Simpson selection comes as Stafford and the Rams [work on an extension](https://x.com/RapSheet/status/2046298248176951790?s=20) to his contract beyond the 2026 season. Los Angeles was most commonly expected to pick __Makai Lemon__, and it was projected to draft a WR (66%) or an offensive lineman (22%) in 88% of expert mock drafts. Stafford could’ve used another weapon in a thin receiving corps behind __Puka Nacua__ and __Davante Adams__, and his star receivers have off-the-field and injury concerns, respectively. __Sean McVay__ even appeared to be less than thrilled about the Simpson selection during a press conference at the end of Day 1. Los Angeles did have an urgent need for a backup quarterback, with __Jimmy Garoppolo__ set to potentially retire, but it could have addressed the spot later in the draft. Stafford is set to regress off his MVP season based on his early ADP (101.3, QB15), and he has a lot more downside if Puka or Davante miss extended time with __Jordan Whittington__, __Konata Mumpfield__, and __Xavier Smith__ filling out the rest of the depth chart.

__{{Jayden Daniels|QB|WAS|23235}}__ (Was) — The Commanders had the chance to select __Jordan Tyson__ or another skill position player at No. 7 to improve Daniels’ extremely weak supporting cast. They instead elected to build up __Dan Quinn__’s underachieving defense by selecting __Sonny Styles__. __Treylon Burks__ is currently the #2 WR behind __Terry McLaurin__, and they were unable to significantly upgrade until landing Clemson’s __Antonio Williams__ in the third round. McLaurin’s top lieutenant isn’t currently on the roster, but it’s expected to be __Brandon Aiyuk__, who is still engaged in a pissing match with the 49ers. The last time we saw Aiyuk, he mustered a miserable 8.9 FPG before suffering a season-ending knee injury seven games into the 2024 season. Aiyuk required two surgeries for a torn ACL and MCL, and he ultimately decided not to play in 2026. Daniels is coming off an injury-riddled sophomore season, in which he appeared in just seven games because of knee, hamstring, and elbow injuries. The Commanders are asking Daniels to carry this offense under new OC __David Blough__, and his ADP is a bit rich (63, QB4) at this point, given his lack of playmakers.

__{{Malik Willis|QB|MIA|23118}}__ (Mia) — Willis took a stack of money ($45 million guaranteed) from the Dolphins for his first real chance at a starting job, but Miami isn’t putting him in a position to succeed. __Greg Dulcich__, __Jalen Tolbert__, and __Malik Washington__ entered the draft at the top of Miami’s receiver depth chart. They remained there after the draft, with the Dolphins reaching for Dane Brugler’s WR31 __Caleb Douglas__ in the third round. They followed that pick up by selecting Louisville’s __Chris Bell__ later in the third round, who is recovering from a torn ACL he suffered in late November. Willis was the best fantasy quarterback when he was on the field last season, scoring 52.2 FP on just 47 dropbacks for an incredible 1.11 FP/DB. He’s capable of creating on his own, but the Dolphins are asking him to work with the NFL’s worst receivers. Willis has potential league-winning upside if he continues to run a lot and if Miami’s defense forces him to play in some high-scoring games, but the lack of offensive talent around him gives him an ugly floor, as well.

__{{Jacoby Brissett|QB|ARI}}__ (Ari) — Brissett is trying to get a pay raise before the 2026 season — he’s set to make $4.88 million this season, with just $1.5 million guaranteed — but the Cardinals are treating him like just another player in a three-man quarterback battle. Arizona handed __Gardner Minshew__ $5.14 million in guaranteed money in free agency before selecting Miami’s __Carson Beck__ at No. 65. Dane Brugler described Beck as a cerebral pocket passer, but his play breaks down when the offense gets out of rhythm. Brissett has the slight leg up on Beck and Minshew to be the Week 1 starter, but the three QBs will battle it out in training camp. All three QBs are good bets to make starts this season as the Cardinals start their March for Arch (Manning).

### RUNNING BACKS

__{{Tyler Allgeier|RB|ARI|23250}}__ and __{{James Conner|RB|ARI|18983}}__ (Ari) — Allgeier bolted from Atlanta to get away from one of the NFL’s best running backs. Unfortunately, the Cardinals ruined Allgeier’s plans to be a lead back by selecting Notre Dame’s __Jeremiyah Love__ at No. 3. Love came in as Brett Whitefield’s [third-best RB](https://www.fantasypoints.com/nfl/prospect-guide/profiles/rookie/rb#/) in his 11 years of scouting, behind only __Christian McCaffrey__ and __Bijan Robinson__. Allgeier finds himself in a similar role to the one he just held behind Bijan for the last three seasons. He’ll likely spell Love for a series in each half and try to pry the limited goal-line opportunities away from Love. Conner and __Trey Benson__ are obvious cut or trade candidates before the start of the season, and this backfield needs to be thinned out to condense the touches with Love and Allgeier moving forward. Allgeier’s ADP (88, RB30) is set to plummet, and he’s back to being a weaker handcuff option because of his limited receiving production on one of the NFL’s worst teams.

__{{Emmanuel Wilson|RB|SEA|24173}} and {{Zach Chabonnet|RB|SEA|23643}}__ (Sea) — The Seahawks entered the draft with just four selections, but there was no chance they were leaving it without using one of those picks on a running back. They lost __Kenneth Walker__ at the start of free agency, and Charbonnet is set to miss the start of the season after tearing his ACL in the middle of January. Seattle’s only significant move to the backfield was the addition of Wilson, a reserve RB for the Packers last season. The Seahawks didn’t waste time remedying the backfield by selecting Notre Dame’s __Jadarian Price__ with the final pick of the first round. It wasn’t a total surprise since Price [reminded](https://www.fantasypoints.com/nfl/prospect-guide/profiles/rookie/rb#/) Brett Whitefield of __Kenneth Walker__ because of his vision, burst, and ability to create beyond his blocking. GM __John Schneider__ admitted after Day 1 that they tried to trade down from No. 32 to collect more picks, but they didn’t want to move far enough down where they wouldn’t have a shot to select Price in the second round. Wilson went from being a potential zero-RB stud while Charbonnet missed time to start the season to being the insurance plan behind a rookie RB who lacks experience as the top option after playing behind __Jeremiyah Love__ the last two seasons.

__{{R.J. Harvey|RB|DEN}}__ and __{{J.K. Dobbins|RB|DEN|21674}}__ (Den) — Denver’s running game hit the skids after Dobbins suffered a Lisfranc injury on a hip-drop tackle in the middle of last season. Denver averaged 4.76 YPC and 128.6 rushing YPG with a 48.1% success rate with Dobbins in the lineup through the first 10 games. It plummeted to 3.80 YPC and 97.9 rushing YPG with a 2.6% explosive run rate in the final nine games with Harvey leading the backfield (postseason included). The Broncos gave Dobbins $8 million guaranteed in free agency to return as the team’s lead runner, and they drafted a potential backup plan in Washington’s __Jonah Coleman__ in the fourth round if Dobbins once again has issues staying healthy. Brett Whitefield [described](https://www.fantasypoints.com/nfl/prospect-guide/profiles/rookie/rb#/) Coleman as a do-it-all back who should work in a timeshare as a change-of-pace runner. __Sean Payton__ loves his backfield timeshares, and there’s a potentially ugly one brewing in Denver. Dobbins is more appealing at his ADP (93.5, RB32) than the overpriced Harvey (68.4, RB26), but this backfield could be frustrating all year if Coleman creates a committee by earning weekly carries.

### RECEIVERS

__{{Harold Fannin|WR|CLE|25870}}__ and __{{Jerry Jeudy|WR|CLE|21692}}__ (Cle) — The Browns owned a pair of first-round picks and had a dire need at WR entering the draft after doing nothing to improve their receiving corps in free agency. It came as no surprise when they selected Texas A&M’s __K.C. Concepcion__ at No. 24, who will immediately compete to be the #1 WR. The Browns weren’t done adding quality WR competition, selecting Washington’s __Denzel Boston__ at No. 39 after he slid out of the first round. Jeudy is coming off a massively disappointing season, averaging just 1.09 YPRR on a 19% TPRR share while competing against greats like __Isaiah Bond__ and __Cedric Tillman__ for WR targets. Brett Whitefield [saw](https://www.fantasypoints.com/nfl/prospect-guide/profiles/rookie/wr) shades of __Brandon Aiyuk__ in Concepcion because of his dynamic ability after the catch, and Boston brings technique, toughness, and strength to the WR room. Fantasy gamers are better off ignoring Jeudy’s existence, even at his depressed ADP (157.8, WR63). Our bigger concern is for Fannin, who suddenly has viable target competition after being the clear #1 receiver as a rookie. Concepcion will eventually compete with Fannin to be the #1 option in Cleveland’s passing game, and Boston also lowers his target ceiling. The Browns will use more 11 personnel after ranking 27th last season (43.9%), which has the potential to pull Fannin off the field a little more. Fannin is more dependent on volume than most TEs, and there could be a little less of it to go around after Cleveland selected two WRs early.

__{{Ricky Pearsall|WR|SF|24982}}__ (SF) — The 49ers have completely overhauled their receiving corps this offseason, starting by prying __Mike Evans__ away from the Buccaneers after 12 years. They also signed veteran __Christian Kirk__ and are planning on letting __Jauan Jennings__ and __Brandon Aiyuk__ walk. San Francisco then stunned the league by selecting an older prospect in Ole Miss’ __De’Zhaun Stribling__ with the first pick of the second round. Brett Whitefield wrote that Stribling has a limited overall skill set, but he’s an “alpha dog” as a run blocker, which will earn him playing time in a __Kyle Shanahan__ offense. Pearsall is entering a make-or-break season as a third-year player, having played in just 20 of his first 34 games (59%). San Francisco will still give him a chance to be the #2 WR behind Evans, but the 49ers now have a backup plan if he lets them down again.

__{{Brenton Strange|TE|JAX|24223}}__ and __{{Parker Washington|WR|JAX}}__ (Jax) — The NFL started to shift toward more 12 personnel (2 TEs) and less 11 personnel (3 WRs) last season. It appears that trend will continue with seven TEs selected in the first 73 picks and nine total TEs selected on the first two days of the draft. The Jaguars surprised the league by selecting Texas A&M’s __Nate Boerkircher__ as the third TE at No. 56, who comes to the NFL with just 417 receiving yards over 52 games in his five-year college career. GM __James Gladstone__ [explained](https://x.com/actionsportsjax/status/2047895869756727560?s=46) the decision to select Boerkircher as “the trend in the NFL is that heavier TE sets were going to be something that was prioritized.” The Jaguars ranked seventh in 11 personnel rate at 66% last season, and Washington is most likely to lose snaps over __Jakobi Meyers__ and __Brian Thomas__ when the Jaguars use two-TE personnel. Strange and Washington will both have more competition for snaps and targets as the Penn State products enter their contract years.

__{{Dallas Goedert|TE|PHI}}__ (Phi) — The Eagles have slowly been pushing Goedert toward the door since last offseason, but he stuck around after taking another pay cut for the second straight year. The Eagles selected his eventual replacement in Vanderbilt’s __Eli Stowers__ at No. 54, much like the Eagles did when they selected Goedert 49th overall in 2018 to be the protege to __Zach Ertz__. Brett Whitefield [called](https://www.fantasypoints.com/nfl/prospect-guide/profiles/rookie/te#/) Stowers a big-time weapon because of his versatility, ball skills, and after-the-catch abilities. Goedert has significantly more target and snap competition from Stowers and first-round pick __Makai Lemon__ in the middle of the field. Goedert’s touchdown production is likely to regress after he more than doubled his touchdown total from any season in his first seven years by scoring a position-best 11 TDs. He also wasn’t the same player with the ball in his hands. His YPR dipped into the single digits for the first time in his career, and his 4.13 YAC/REC was his lowest mark in the Fantasy Points Data era. Goedert is moving in the wrong direction, even with __A.J. Brown__ likely out of the picture. There are better bets at the position than Goedert at his current ADP (133.8, TE14).

__{{Mason Taylor|TE|NYJ|25963}}__ and __{{Adonai Mitchell|WR|NYJ|24954}}__ (NYJ) — The Jets were expected to target a receiver with their second pick in the first round, but they left Day 1 of the draft with a pair of receivers by jumping back into the tail end of the first round. They took a best-player-available approach when they selected Oregon’s __Kenyon Sadiq__ at No. 16 over __Makai Lemon__. They still got a WR in Indiana’s __Omar Cooper__ at No. 30. Brett Whitefield [described](https://www.fantasypoints.com/nfl/prospect-guide/profiles/rookie/wr#/) Sadiq as a mutant who has the necessary receiving chops to be one of the NFL’s top TEs, and Cooper is a run-after-catch demon who is reminiscent of __D.J. Moore__. Taylor will battle Sadiq for early-down snaps to start the season, but Sadiq’s selection is a clear indictment of the 2025 second-round pick. Taylor is no longer on the fantasy radar, but he’s likely to be a thorn in Sadiq’s fantasy outlook as a rookie. Mitchell is still an intriguing late-round dart throw (176.5, WR69), but it’s going to be more difficult to pop for a couple of big games with Sadiq and Cooper also competing for targets behind __Garrett Wilson__.

__Kansas City Chiefs Passing Game__ (KC) — Kansas City’s days of being the league’s most pass-heavy team could be coming to an end. The Chiefs have ranked inside the top two spots in pass rate over expectation in each of the last five seasons, but they’ve committed to running the ball and to playing better defense this offseason. The Chiefs passed on upgrading Mahomes’ offensive line and his receiving corps through the first two days of the draft by selecting three defensive players inside the top-40 picks. Kansas City also finally had enough of its pathetic rushing attack, handing __Kenneth Walker__ $28.7 million guaranteed in free agency to balance its offense. __Patrick Mahomes__ will be in a race to be ready for the start of the season off his ACL and LCL in mid-December, and it wouldn’t be surprising if he gets off to a sluggish start. They signed the run-heavy __Justin Fields__ to be in his fill-in if he’s not ready for September, and he’s had limited passing games at every stop in his NFL career.

__Tennessee Titans WRs__ — The Titans pulled a mild stunner at No. 4 when they selected Ohio State’s __Carnell Tate__, which gives __Cam Ward__ two new top targets. They previously signed __Wan’Dale Robinson__ $38 million guaranteed contract at the start of free agency. Tate will step into a prominent role immediately, and he’ll challenge Robinson for the most targets from Ward. Brett Whitefield [ranked](https://www.fantasypoints.com/nfl/prospect-guide/profiles/rookie/wr#/) Tate directly between __A.J. Brown__ and __CeeDee Lamb__ as a top-10 WR evaluation in his decade of scouting college prospects. __Chimere Dike__ and __Elic Ayomanor__ previously occupied large roles as rookies last season, but they’ll be competing with __Calvin Ridley__ for the #3 WR snap and targets. Ridley owned a solid 23% TPRR when he was on the field, but just 70.6% of his targets were catchable early in Ward’s rookie season. Dike (196.8, WR79) and Ayomanor (227.4, WR91) are now off the radar in fantasy drafts, and Ridley barely has a pulse (170.9, WR67) as a late-round dart. Robinson is still a safe floor pick at an ADP that is likely to dip a bit (104.6, WR47), but it’s tough to build an upside case for him with Tate battling him for targets.

__{{Terrance Ferguson|TE|LAR|25970}}__ (LAR) — The Rams passed on __Makai Lemon__ to select __Ty Simpson__ at No. 13, and they selected yet another TE in Ohio State’s __Max Klare__ with their next pick in the second round instead of adding to their extremely thin WR corps. The Rams already have Ferguson, __Colby Parkinson__, __Tyler Higbee__, and __Davis Allen__ under contract for 2026. Los Angeles easily led the league in 13 personnel rate (3 TEs) at 30.5%, which is likely to continue in 2026 with Klare added to the mix. Ferguson or another Rams TE, like Parkinson, could have some fantasy-relevant moments, but they’re going to be far from consistent with so many TEs battling for snaps and targets.
author: Tom Brolley
